text: The coverage floor of the unit and component gate, the duplication limit and the severity cut-off of static analysis are values of the gate-set version and have no value in the source set; a change to any of them is a reviewed change of the gate set that produces the next version, so a service story and a service repository never carry a threshold of their own. Until the values are published the gate set carries them as named keys with no default in code.
why: NFR-054 requires the pipeline to block a change that carries a secret, personal data or an unapproved dependency, and Arch v5 slides 11, 20 and 29 require contract tests and the boundary test in every build, but no source gives a coverage floor, a duplication limit or a severity cut-off; a gate that compares against nothing cannot fail a build, and a per-service number would break the one-gate-set rule of this story.

text: The gate set names each gate by its rule and not by a product: the test runner, the contract checker, the migration linter, the secret and personal-data scanner, the dependency and licence source, the image scanner and the static-analysis engine behind the eight gates are values of the gate configuration, chosen by the DevOps lead with the security architect, so that a product change is a configuration change of the gate set and no service story changes. The reporting surface of the baseline is the release report of RWB-PLT-NF01-OPS — one report per release, one row per changed service and gate, with the state, the gate-set version, the build record reference and the exception in force — and no new Workbench screen is created.
why: NFR-054 and Arch v5 slides 11, 29 and 35 fix what must be checked and not what checks it, and no source names a scanner, a contract checker, a static-analysis engine or a licence source; the same silence covers the reporting surface, which the baseline must still place so that the platform administrator has one place to read a release.

text: An exception is recorded with its gate, service, commit or image digest, owner role, reason, expiry date and approver role, and the pipeline expires it into a failure on its expiry date with no further action and no renewal without a new recorded exception; the length of the box, the approver role and the set of gates marked non-waivable are values of the gate set. The secret, personal-data and unapproved-dependency gates are blocking by NFR-054 and are not on the waivable list; every other gate may be excepted inside a box.
why: The story must state what an exception is, who owns it and what happens when it lapses, and no source gives a box length, an approver role or a list of non-waivable gates; NFR-054 says the pipeline blocks a change, so a secret, personal-data or unapproved-dependency finding cannot be excepted away, while the other gates need a time-boxed path or a team would disable them instead.

why: The legacy story names both paths and no source gives a target path for the platform template or for a service repository, so the preserved story cannot be tested against the template without one value for each; the as-built value is the only one that a source states.

why: The legacy story has one module map for all 19 modules; no source names the per-service file, its directory or its scope, and the delta story cannot load a map without one value for each.

text: The staging schema of a service is named `<schema>_next` in SIT and UAT, in the pattern of the legacy `recovery_next`, and the loader resolves each table of the extract to one owning service through the Ownership Map plus the per-service database stories, so the per-service layout of the extract is derived from the manifest and that resolution rather than from a layout the source does not define.
why: RWB-TE-004 names only `recovery_next` for one `recovery` schema; the 19-schema target needs one staging schema per service and a rule that maps a table to exactly one service, and no source states either. The load cannot run without both, and inventing a business value is not permitted.
read: RWB-TE-004 section 12 (restart behaviour, staging schema `recovery_next`) and section 13 (database, swap and tool table); Architecture v5 slides 29 and 41; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (table to service owner)
confirm: Solution architect, with the PII extract contract and the P1 source-data contract, before the load is published; the staging suffix is then fixed in `rwb.maskedcopy.staging-suffix`
impact: If the suffix or the resolution changes, the preflight, the staging grants and the swap of section 13 change with it; the checks, the acceptance criteria and the report of this story do not, because they name the service and the schema and never a suffix.

text: The swap runs per service, one service at a time, in the order held in `rwb.maskedcopy.swap-order` (the 19 services in the order of their code, `rwb_access` first and `rwb_writeoff` last), under one advisory lock per environment; every swap starts only after the checks of all 19 services have passed, the previous copy of each schema is retained until the last swap succeeds, and a swap that fails is restored from the retained copy so the estate is never mixed.
why: RWB-TE-004 swaps one schema in one step (`recovery_next` renamed to `recovery`); it fixes neither an order nor a lock for 19 swaps, and Arch v5 slide 29 names no swap mechanism. A fixed order and one lock are needed so two runs cannot interleave and so the report and the restore path are deterministic.
read: RWB-TE-004 section 13 (advisory lock per environment; swap after the checks); Architecture v5 slide 29 (one login and one schema per service; no cross-schema key)
confirm: Solution architect and the ACE database administrator, before the load is published; the order is then a configuration value and the swap itself stays one rename per service
impact: A different order or a single all-schema swap changes the swap component and the restore path of section 13 and the state table of section 9; the refusal rule, the report and the acceptance criteria that no service is swapped while another fails stay as written.

text: The tool record lives in the table `masked_copy_load` in schema `tools`, outside the 19 service schemas, and until the personal-data field registry operation of RWB-P1-E1065-CON is published the loader takes the field list from `sys_fields.is_personal` of `rwb_source_data` read through that owner's contract; the loader reads no service table directly.
why: RWB-TE-004 names the table `masked_copy_load` in 'the tool's own schema `tools`' for a monolith with one recovery schema, and reads `sys_fields.is_personal` directly. The 19-schema target names 19 service schemas and no tool schema, and the field registry operation is not defined anywhere in the source set, so both values are working defaults rather than copied facts.
read: RWB-TE-004 sections 11, 12 and 13; Architecture v5 slide 29 (the 19 schemas and the logins); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (`sys_fields` owner P1); the plan entry of RWB-P1-E1065-CON
confirm: Solution architect and the P1 rwb-source-data owner, before the load is published; the schema and table are then configuration values `rwb.maskedcopy.tool-schema` and `rwb.maskedcopy.tool-table`
impact: A different tool schema moves one table and the extract-ID check of the manifest validator; a published registry operation replaces the `sys_fields` default with one contract call and leaves the verifier, its patterns and the acceptance criteria unchanged.
